text:
I stood at the edge of the Corrowen Test Loop on 14 March 2031 and watched the Vantry maglev prototype pass at a speed I could feel in my chest before I heard it.

The prototype reached 380 km/h on a 14.2 km stretch of straight guideway, holding that speed for about 11 seconds. Dr. Isela Marwick, Chief Test Engineer at Vantry Transit Systems, supervised the run and confirmed the reading.

"That's the number, and it held," Dr. Marwick told me minutes afterward, still wearing her headset.

The result is documented in Vantry Transit Systems Test Report VT-P2-117, which has been certified by the Halvern Rail Standards Board. The top speed recorded by the Vantry maglev prototype was 380 km/h.

The run was brief, and the train was gone almost as soon as it arrived. The figure, however, now stands on the record.
